stories.actor: Mar Zutra and Rabbi Yehuda from India
stories.event: Mar Zutra visited the dying convert Rabbi Yehuda from India and had the convert's slave carry his shoes home.
stories.turn: Seeing the heirless convert was about to die, Mar Zutra used the slave's labor to acquire him before he could go free.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yehuda died and Mar Zutra gained the slave: one departed to death, the other to life.
stories.summary: Rabbi Yehuda from India, a convert with no heirs, fell ill and Mar Zutra came to visit. Seeing that he was close to death, Mar Zutra told the convert's slave to take off his shoes and carry them to his house, which acquired the slave for him. The convert went to his death and Mar Zutra came away with a slave.

stories.actor: Abaye and his tenant farmer
stories.event: Abaye allowed his tenant farmer to betroth a nursing woman after fifteen months.
stories.turn: Rav Yosef told Abaye that Rav and Shmuel require twenty-four months.
stories.outcome: Abaye ran after the farmer for parasangs but could not catch him, and drew the lesson that one should not rule near one's teacher.
stories.summary: Abaye's tenant farmer asked whether he could betroth a nursing woman after fifteen months, and Abaye said yes. When Abaye told Rav Yosef, Rav Yosef cited Rav and Shmuel, who require a twenty-four month wait. Abaye ran three parasangs after the farmer to stop him but never caught up, and concluded that one should not rule even on a simple matter where one's teacher is.

stories.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua
stories.event: The two sages planned to rule by a baraita that let a nursing mother marry at once if she gave her child to a wet nurse.
stories.turn: An old woman told them Rav Nahman had forbidden it in her own case, and Rav Pappi reminded them of Rabbi Meir's decrees.
stories.outcome: They admitted they had forgotten the principle.
stories.summary: Rav Pappa and Rav Huna were about to rule that a nursing mother who had handed her child to a wet nurse could remarry immediately. An old woman said Rav Nahman had forbidden exactly that to her. Rav Pappi then reminded them that the halakha follows Rabbi Meir's protective decrees, and they admitted the point had slipped their minds.

stories.actor: the daughter-in-law of the house of bar Elyashiv
stories.event: A widow claiming her marriage contract from the orphans was told to dress properly before going to court.
stories.turn: She put on all her clothes, and the clothes she wore then counted against her claim.
stories.outcome: Ravina ruled with Rav that a widow's clothes are appraised and deducted.
stories.summary: A widow of the bar Elyashiv family was taking the orphans to court over her marriage contract. They said it would shame them for her to go in house clothes, so she dressed in all her garments. Ravina then ruled, following Rav, that the court appraises what a widow is wearing, so all those clothes were counted against what she was owed.

stories.actor: a steward of orphans before Abaye
stories.event: A man who had named a field as a boundary marker for someone else later contested it and died, and his orphans' steward took the case to Abaye.
stories.turn: Abaye ruled the claim lost, but the steward offered arguments the father could have made, and Abaye accepted each one.
stories.outcome: The steward kept most of the field, and Abaye praised him as the kind of steward to appoint.
stories.summary: A man had named a field as a marker for another person's field, then contested its ownership and died, leaving a steward for his orphans. Abaye first ruled the claim was lost. The steward argued that the father would have said he meant only one furrow, and then that he had bought that furrow back. Abaye accepted both arguments and said orphans need a steward like this one.

stories.actor: Rav Ashi and Rav Kahana
stories.event: Rav Kahana jogged Rav Ashi's memory about testimony Rav Ashi could not recall.
stories.turn: Rav Ashi later remembered and testified, but Rav Kahana hesitated, fearing he had planted the memory.
stories.outcome: Rav Ashi told him he remembered through his own effort, not on Rav Kahana's word.
stories.summary: Rav Ashi knew some testimony concerning Rav Kahana but at first said he did not remember it, even when Rav Kahana described what happened. In the end Rav Ashi remembered and testified. When he saw Rav Kahana was uneasy about it, he said he was not relying on Rav Kahana; he had worked at it and remembered by himself.

stories.actor: Rav Adda bar Ahava's host and Rav Beivai
stories.event: The host, son of a convert, and Rav Beivai quarreled over who would hold office in the city.
stories.turn: Rav Yosef ruled that converts may not hold office, but Rav Adda asked about a Jewish-born mother.
stories.outcome: Since the host's mother was born Jewish, the duties were divided between the two, and Abaye praised Rav Adda for pleading his host's case.
stories.summary: Rav Adda bar Ahava's host, a convert's son, and Rav Beivai each wanted to take charge of the city's affairs. Rav Yosef ruled that every appointment must come from among your brothers, which seemed to rule out the host. Rav Adda asked whether that held when the mother was Jewish-born, and Rav Yosef said it did not. So Rav Beivai took the religious matters and the host the civic ones, and Abaye said a scholar should host someone like Rav Adda, who argues for him.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yonatan, Rabbi Hanina and a grateful man
stories.event: A man bowed and kissed Rabbi Yonatan's foot in front of Rabbi Hanina.
stories.turn: Rabbi Hanina asked why, and Rabbi Yonatan explained the man had signed his property over to his sons.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yonatan had forced the sons to support their father.
stories.summary: While Rabbi Hanina and Rabbi Yonatan stood together, a man came, bent down and kissed Rabbi Yonatan's foot. Asked what that was about, Rabbi Yonatan said the man had written his property over to his sons, and he had made the sons feed him.

stories.actor: Rabbi Yeshevav (or Rabbi Akiva's friend)
stories.event: A man wanted to give more than a fifth of his property to charity.
stories.turn: His friend refused to let him.
stories.outcome: He was stopped from giving away more than a fifth.
stories.summary: Someone set out to give more than a fifth of his property to charity, and his friend would not let him. In one version the friend was Rabbi Yeshevav; in another, Rabbi Yeshevav was the giver and Rabbi Akiva stopped him.

stories.actor: a woman in Jerusalem and the child she raised
stories.event: A woman came to Jerusalem carrying a child on her shoulders and raised him.
stories.turn: When he grew up he had relations with her.
stories.outcome: The court stoned them both, because his attachment to her gave him the presumed status of her son.
stories.summary: A woman arrived in Jerusalem with a child riding on her shoulders and brought him up. When he grew up he slept with her. They were brought to court and stoned, not because he was proven to be her son, but because the way he had clung to her made him presumptively so.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hananya ben Hakhinai
stories.event: Coming home after years away, he heard a girl called daughter of Hakhinai and followed her home.
stories.turn: His wife looked up, recognized him, and died of the shock.
stories.outcome: He prayed for her and she came back to life.
stories.summary: Ben Hakhinai sat by a river and heard a girl called daughter of Hakhinai, realized she was his own daughter, and followed her home. His wife, sifting flour, looked up and recognized him, and her heart gave out and she died. He asked God whether this was the poor woman's reward, prayed for her, and she lived.

stories.actor: Rabbi Hama bar Bisa
stories.event: After twelve years in the study hall he sent word home first instead of walking in unannounced.
stories.turn: He met a sharp young scholar without knowing it was his own son, and later stood up for him at home.
stories.outcome: His wife pointed out that he was standing for his son, Rabbi Oshaya.
stories.summary: Rabbi Hama bar Bisa studied away from home for twelve years and, to avoid ben Hakhinai's mistake, went to the local study hall and sent word home. A young man, his son Rabbi Oshaya, questioned him there with such sharpness that Rabbi Hama regretted not having raised a son like that. When the son followed him home, Rabbi Hama stood up for him as for a scholar, and his wife asked whether a father stands up for his son.

stories.actor: Rabbi Akiva and the daughter of ben Kalba Savua
stories.event: The rich man's daughter married the shepherd Akiva in secret on condition he go to study, and her father disowned her.
stories.turn: Akiva returned after twelve years, overheard her say she would wait twelve more, and left again, coming back with twenty-four thousand students.
stories.outcome: He honored his wife publicly, and her father, learning who Akiva was, kissed his feet and gave him half his wealth.
stories.summary: Ben Kalba Savua's daughter married his shepherd Akiva in secret and sent him off to study, and her father threw her out and vowed she would get nothing from him. After twelve years Akiva came home and overheard her say she would gladly have him study twelve more, so he went back. When he came home with twenty-four thousand students she fell at his feet, and he told his attendants that everything they and he had was hers. Her father came to ask the great man to annul his vow, learned the man was Akiva, and gave him half his money.

stories.actor: Rav Yosef son of Rava
stories.event: Sent to study for six years, he set out to go home after three, on the eve of Yom Kippur.
stories.turn: His father came out armed to meet him and rebuked him for remembering his wife.
stories.outcome: In the quarrel neither of them ate the last meal before the fast.
stories.summary: Rava sent his son Rav Yosef to study with Rav Yosef for six years. After three years, on the eve of Yom Kippur, the son decided to go home to see his wife. His father heard, took a weapon and went out to meet him, asking whether he had remembered his mistress, or in another version his dove. They were so caught up in the argument that neither ate the meal before the fast.

stories.actor: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi
stories.event: The three sat at the gate of King Izgur's house as the king's butler passed by carrying food.
stories.turn: Rav Ashi noticed something about Mar Zutra (cut off at the window's edge).
stories.outcome: Not shown; the window ends.
stories.summary: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi were sitting at the entrance of King Izgur's house when the king's chief butler walked by with food. Rav Ashi saw something in Mar Zutra's face, and the story continues past the end of the window.

stories.actor: a father, mother, and the father's relative
stories.event: The parents argued over which of their relatives would marry their minor daughter, and the mother wore the father down until he agreed to hers.
stories.turn: During the engagement meal the father's relative climbed onto the roof and betrothed the girl himself.
stories.outcome: His betrothal was the one that happened (the Gemara then argues whether the father wanted it).
stories.summary: A father wanted his minor daughter to marry his relative, the mother wanted her own relative, and she pressed him until he agreed to her choice. While everyone was eating and drinking at the festive meal, the father's relative went up on the roof and betrothed the girl to himself.

stories.actor: Shmuel's father, Shmuel and Shmuel's daughters
stories.event: Shmuel's father set guards over redeemed captive women in Neharde'a, and when Shmuel objected he asked whether Shmuel would treat his own daughters so.
stories.turn: Shmuel's own daughters were later taken captive and brought to Eretz Yisrael.
stories.outcome: They declared themselves pure before their captors came in, were permitted to marry priests, and Rabbi Hanina told the priest Rav Shemen to marry one of them.
stories.summary: When captive women were brought to Neharde'a, Shmuel's father posted guards over them. Shmuel asked what the point was, and his father asked whether he would slight them like that if they were his daughters. The words came true: Shmuel's daughters were captured and taken to Eretz Yisrael, where they left their captors outside, entered Rabbi Hanina's study hall, and each said she had been captive and was pure, so they were permitted. Rabbi Hanina saw they must be daughters of scholars, it came out that they were Shmuel's, and he told the priest Rav Shemen bar Abba to go and marry one of his relatives.

stories.actor: a blind man who studied with Mar Shmuel
stories.event: Mar Shmuel sent a messenger to look for the blind man when he was late, and the two missed each other on the way.
stories.turn: The messenger came back saying he had seen the blind man's wife commit adultery.
stories.outcome: Mar Shmuel told the blind man to divorce her if he trusted the messenger, and not to otherwise.
stories.summary: A blind man who reviewed mishnayot for Mar Shmuel was late one day, so Shmuel sent a messenger after him. The messenger went by one road while the blind man arrived by another, and at the house the messenger saw the wife committing adultery. When the blind man asked, Shmuel told him to divorce her if he believed the messenger, and otherwise not to.

stories.actor: King Yannai, Elazar ben Po'ira and the Sages
stories.event: Celebrating a victory, Yannai held a feast for the Sages, and Elazar ben Po'ira told him the Pharisees secretly opposed him.
stories.turn: When Yehuda ben Gedidya told Yannai to give up the priesthood because of a rumor about his mother, Elazar urged him to crush the Sages.
stories.outcome: The Sages were killed and Torah was forgotten until Shimon ben Shatah restored it.
stories.summary: After conquering sixty cities, King Yannai gathered the Sages to a feast. The scoundrel Elazar ben Po'ira told him the Pharisees resented him and had him wear the priestly frontplate as a test. The elder Yehuda ben Gedidya told Yannai to be content with the crown and leave the priesthood, since people said his mother had been a captive. The rumor could not be proven and the Sages were driven out in anger, and Elazar then pushed Yannai to destroy them. All the Sages were killed and the world was empty of Torah until Shimon ben Shatah restored it.

stories.actor: a man who rented a donkey
stories.event: A man rented out his donkey on condition that the renter avoid the watery Pekod River route.
stories.turn: The renter took that route anyway and the donkey died.
stories.outcome: Before Rava the renter claimed there had been no water; Rava believed him, but Abaye objected that the claim goes against known facts.
stories.summary: A man rented his donkey to a friend and told him to take the dry Neresh road, not the Pekod River road where there is water. The renter took the river road and the donkey died. Before Rava he admitted taking that road but said there was no water there. Rava believed him, since he could just as easily have lied about the road, but Abaye said that argument does not work against known facts.

stories.actor: a man who sold his property to move to Eretz Yisrael
stories.event: A man sold his property, saying it was so he could move to Eretz Yisrael.
stories.turn: He went but could not settle there, came back, and tried to cancel the sale.
stories.outcome: Rava ruled that the sale could be canceled (or, in another version, that it could not).
stories.summary: A man sold everything he owned, saying he was moving to Eretz Yisrael. He went but could not manage to settle there, and when he came back he wanted the sale undone. Rava ruled that a person goes up in order to settle, so the sale could be cancelled. Another version has Rava ruling the other way: he meant to go up, he went, and the sale stands.

stories.actor: a Madonite in Jerusalem
stories.event: A dying Madonite wanted to give away many movable goods and was told he could only do it by means of land.
stories.turn: He bought a rocky plot near Jerusalem and transferred the goods along with portions of it.
stories.outcome: He died and the Sages carried out his gifts.
stories.summary: A Madonite in Jerusalem with many movable goods wanted to give them away, and the Sages told him the only way was to transfer them by means of land. He bought a small plot near Jerusalem and declared that its northern part, along with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, went to a certain person. He died, and the Sages upheld what he had said.

stories.actor: a man in Jerusalem
stories.event: A man in Jerusalem wanted to give away many movable goods and was told he could only do it by means of land.
stories.turn: He bought a small plot and gave one square handbreadth of it, along with the goods, to the recipient.
stories.outcome: He died and the Sages carried out his gift.
stories.summary: A man in Jerusalem, sick in one version and healthy in another, wanted to give away a large amount of movable property. Told he could only do so by means of land, he bought a beit rova near the city and gave a square handbreadth of it, along with a hundred sheep and a hundred barrels, to someone. He died, and the Sages upheld his words.

stories.actor: Rabbi Zeira and Rava in Mehoza
stories.event: Rabbi Zeira taught in Mehoza that a convert may marry a mamzeret, and the many converts there pelted him with their etrogim.
stories.turn: Rava taught that a convert may marry a priest's daughter and was carried on silk, then taught that a convert may also marry a mamzeret.
stories.outcome: When the people said he had spoiled his first teaching, Rava answered that he had given them both options.
stories.summary: Rabbi Zeira taught in Mehoza, a town full of converts, that a convert may marry a mamzeret, and the crowd pelted him with etrogim. Rava said no one should teach that in such a place, and he himself taught that a convert may marry a priest's daughter, and they carried him on silk. When he then also taught that a convert may marry a mamzeret and they complained, he said he had done them a favor: a convert can marry from either group.

stories.actor: Ze'eiri and Rabbi Yohanan
stories.event: Ze'eiri kept avoiding Rabbi Yohanan, who wanted him to marry his daughter.
stories.turn: When Ze'eiri carried Rabbi Yohanan across a puddle, Rabbi Yohanan asked why his Torah was good enough but his daughters were not.
stories.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan argued against the lineage worry, though the Gemara notes he had missed that Ezra purified Babylonia.
stories.summary: Ze'eiri, a Babylonian, kept dodging Rabbi Yohanan, who kept urging him to marry his daughter. One day on the road Ze'eiri carried Rabbi Yohanan across a puddle on his shoulders, and Rabbi Yohanan asked why his Torah was fit for honor but his daughters were not fit to marry. He argued that flawed families had stayed behind in Babylonia just as fit ones had, though the Gemara says he had overlooked the teaching that Ezra left Babylonia only after making it like fine flour.

stories.actor: Ulla and Rav Yehuda
stories.event: Visiting Rav Yehuda in Pumbedita, Ulla saw that his grown son Rav Yitzhak was unmarried.
stories.turn: Rav Yehuda said he did not know where to find a wife of sound lineage for him.
stories.outcome: Ulla answered that no one can be sure of his own lineage (the window ends during his reply).
stories.summary: Ulla came to Rav Yehuda's house in Pumbedita and saw that Rav Yehuda's son was grown but unmarried. Rav Yehuda said he did not know where to find him a wife, because he worried about lineage. Ulla asked whether any of them knew where they came from, since they might be descended from the ravished women of Zion, and went on making the point.

stories.actor: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva
stories.event: A ritual bath in Yavne presumed to be full was measured and found short, raising the question of the purifications done in it.
stories.turn: Tarfon declared them pure and Akiva impure, and they argued it out through parables.
stories.outcome: Akiva's reasoning won, and Tarfon praised him: whoever leaves you leaves life.
stories.summary: The reservoir of Diskim in Yavne was thought to hold enough water for immersion, but when measured it came up short. Rabbi Tarfon ruled that everything purified in it was still pure, and Rabbi Akiva that it was impure, and they argued over whether the case was like a priest found to be a divorcee's son or one found to have a blemish. Akiva showed that the bath, like the blemish, is disqualified by a single witness and by its own condition. Tarfon accepted this and told him that anyone who parts from him parts from life.

stories.actor: a man in Mata Mehasya and his brother
stories.event: A man due to marry his late brother's widow found his other brother trying to disqualify her from him with a bill of divorce.
stories.turn: He offered to split the estate, but the brother feared being cheated like the swindler from Pumbedita.
stories.outcome: He offered to divide the property right away (the Gemara then asks whether that transfer could take effect).
stories.summary: In Mata Mehasya a man was due to marry his late brother's widow, and another brother wanted to disqualify her from him by giving her a bill of divorce. The man asked whether this was about the property and offered to split it. The brother said he was afraid of being cheated the way the Pumbedita swindler had cheated someone, so the man offered to divide it with him from that moment.
